summary: Directory pairs an Adel lookout in Cook County with the Georgia Forestry Commission; the Georgia list has an adel GFC entry there. No source describes the site today.

evidence.supports: Directory Adel entry gives Cook County and the Georgia Forestry Commission
List entry adel GFC: Cook County, coordinates, and a value of 232 in the elevation column
The list says its names for towers numbered 73 and above are the compiler's own
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

notes_for_editor: The Georgia list has two Adel entries: GA237 'adel' (gfc-815), covered by research/us-ga-adel.json, and GA309 'adel GFC' (this record). The directory has two Adel pages (adel.html and adel-gfc.html), both giving Cook County - Georgia Forestry Commission, and the pages cannot tell us which list entry each one describes; the agency fact rests on that directory text. The BLL-41128 code in the list is one of the list's BLL-nnn codes; the list says GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers under that scheme, so the brief's register 'BLL US 41128' may be a list code rather than a register. Left out of facts for that reason. The list's 232 has no unit. A Georgia Forestry Commission Cook County annual report (cookcountyga.us, FY20) was read and does not mention a tower. Two searches found no build, staffing or fate history. The story is about 87 words, below the 120-word floor, because no further evidence was found.
